original_source_text: Driven by the dominance of AI workloads and the resulting pressure on in-core SRAM, shared memory serves as a critical intermediate buffer in GPUs. We observe substantial data redundancy, with up to 60.2% of subsequent memory requests reaccessing data already loaded into shared memory. This redundancy remains largely underexplored, increasing bandwidth demands. We propose Nash, a lightweight mechanism that tracks data provenance via a Source Location Table (SLT) to detect and redirect redundant requests within or across neighboring SMs. Cycle-accurate simulation shows Nash achieves up to 18.3% performance improvement, 9.8% energy savings, and 25.3% reduction in global memory traffic.
